thread:
Sam: Heads-up — we're seeing persistent 429s for customer cus-231 after the EU ingress cutover. Started ~09:12 UTC and hasn't recovered.
Sam: Sample error: `{"error":"quota_exceeded","reason":"burst_window"}`. Appears intermittent per host.
Sam: From the logs I'm seeing a mix of scopes in headers: `X-RW-Auth: key=proj:abc123` and `X-Forwarded-For: 35.198.22.14` but the attribution looks like it's falling back to IP.
Sam: Full request header (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/outputs
Host: eu.api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer proj-abc123
X-Org: org-77
X-Forwarded-For: 35.198.22.14
```
thread_addendum:
Priya: thx Sam. Can you confirm if the customer is behind a NAT (cloud NAT or on-prem)? if so, is there a stable egress IP or a pool?
Priya: Also, did they switch to EU-only keys or are they using the same global API key?
Sam: They're on GCP, using a Cloud NAT with 5 ephemeral egress IPs. They rotated key -> same project-scoped key (proj-abc123).
SRE Bot: [alert] RateLimit spike for cus-231 at 09:12:15 UTC - 429s increased 420% over baseline. Auto-detected scope: mixed (ip + key).
Dan: I'm looking at rate diagnostics for proj-abc123. I'm seeing many short bursts from multiple clients that share 35.198.22.0/24. Our scope heuristic seems to prefer IP when key metadata is ambiguous.
Dan: Can you paste one full 429 response headers from the customer? need `x-rw-*` headers (eg `x-rw-limit-scope`, `x-rw-retry-after`).
Sam: here's a recorded response we got:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-limit-scope: ip
x-rw-retry-after: 3
x-rw-quota: 120/60s
content-type: application/json
```
Priya: aha — `x-rw-limit-scope: ip` means attribution used ingress IP bucket. That explains why multiple projects sharing NAT are contending.
Claire: Two likely edgecases: (1) our auth fallthrough picks IP when request order has `Authorization` after some proxy header rewrite, (2) a TTL 'sticky' binding in the NAT keeps the customer's ephemeral IP sticky to another project key in our attribution cache.
Dan: quick repro for us: curl sample that should trigger same path (you can swap IP with `--resolve` or run from a VM behind Cloud NAT):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer proj-abc123" -H "X-Org: org-77" https://eu.api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
Priya: short-term workaround: rotate to an org-scoped key or use a dedicated project key pinned to a single egress IP (if they can reserve one). That will force attribution by key/org instead of IP.
Sam: tried org-scoped key — that dropped 429s immediately (small sample).
Claire: long-term: we should tweak the attribution TTL and precedence. Proposed: prefer `Authorization`/org key when present and only use IP as fallback if auth fails or header missing, plus decrease sticky TTL from 2h -> 5m for NAT ranges.
Dan: I'll open an infra ticket to adjust heuristic and add a canary to EU region so we don't regress.
Priya: also need a KB article: "Why NAT/shared IPs trigger 429s and how to mitigate" — include steps: reserve static egress IP, use org-scoped key, add `X-Project` header, request quota bump for burst windows.
Sam: customer acceptance: they've reserved a static egress IP and switched to org key; monitoring shows requests normalized. I'll follow up if anything else pops. :thumbsup:
Claire: action items -> INFRA-4334 adjust fallthrough precedence, DOCS-221 add KB, SUPPORT-987 customer remediation steps. Assigning Dan, Priya, Sam.
SRE Bot: [resolved] Alert for cus-231 suppressed at 09:26:40 UTC after mitigation steps.
Sam: thanks all — keeping this thread pinned to the case.
